clusters.state_of_play: IndyCar's Freedom 250 Grand Prix on Washington DC's National Mall concluded Sunday, marking the country's 250th anniversary and serving as the final major event of the celebrations; Kyle Kirkwood won the race (his second win of the 2026 season) after holding off the field, with Alex Palou starting from pole on the 1.7-mile street circuit. Trump performed a ceremonial lap in 'the Beast' before waving the green flag - initially struggling to hold it correctly until corrected by Melania Trump and Command Sgt Maj Matt Williams - then greeted drivers; DC Mayor Muriel Bowser served as grand marshal. Melania Trump attended alongside aide Natalie Harp and son Eric Trump, marking Melania's second public appearance this week. A scary crash occurred on Lap 36 when David Malukas clipped the inside wall and Sting Ray Robb T-boned his stopped car. Nolan Siegel, Marcus Ericsson, and Mick Schumacher had faced six-place grid penalties for engine changes. The event drew large crowds along a route past the Capitol Building and down Pennsylvania Avenue, with drivers reaching speeds up to 185 mph, though attendees faced logistical chaos including long water lines amid sweltering heat. The White House also faced online accusations of plagiarizing promotional graphics, allegedly resembling Rolex 24 race materials.
